full_judgment:
Siddiqur Rahman Miah, J: This Rule on an application filed under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure was issued calling upon the opposite parties to show cause as to why the impugned proceedings of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan case No. 275 of 2008 arising out of complaint petition case No. 159 of 2008 under section 11 (Gha)/30 of the Nari-O-Shihsu Nirjatan Daman Ain, 2000 now pending in the court of learned Nari-o-Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Cox's Bazar should not be quashed. 

 2. The prosecution case, in brief, is that the opposite party No.2, Ismat Ara Bulbul being complainant filed a petitioner of complaint before Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Daman Tribunal, Cox's Bazar alleging, inter alia, that she is Muslim Lady. She was married with accused petitioner No.1 Md. Ehsanullah out of love and affection. The accused petitioner No.1 is a loafer and dowry hunter and other accused petitioners are also imposter and not respectful to the law and order of the state. At the conjugal life, initially they were happy. But when the accused no.1 demanded dowry then their conjugal life be the bitter. The complainant gave Taka 1,00,000 + 50,000 + 50,000 consecutively to the accused petitioner No.1 as dowry for her happiness in conjugal life Later on when the complainant denied to give further dowry to the accused petitioner No. 1, he being irritant frequently beaten the complainant, in this way the complainant has been passing hellish life with her husband. Her husband always used to claim dowry and beaten the complainant. There was salish regarding the matter. But everything was failed due to undue influence by the accused petitioners. So the complainant filed this complaint petition for taking legal action. Thereafter the case was made enquiry by the enquiry agency and submitted report. All the accused petitioners have been enlarged on bail. The tribunal was pleased to frame charge on 29.04.2009 against the accused petitioner rejecting the discharge petition. 

 4. Mr. SM Salim, the learned Advocate for the petitioner submits that the complainant filed earlier a complaint petitioner being no. 1109 of 2007 before the learned Magistrate court which was also withdrawn and that the complainant have been filing case one after another against the accused petitioners just to harass and humiliate them in the society. He further submits that the section as alleged by the complainant does not tenable in the eye of law as such the alleged proceedings is liable to be quashed in the interest of justice. 

 6. The only question that survives for the determination in this case is whether the inherent power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal procedure can be exercised for quashing the proceedings of Nari-O-Shishu Nirjatan case No. 275 of 2008 in setting aside the order of the Additional Metropolitan Sessions Judge dated 29.04.2009. 

 561A Nothing in this case shall be deemed to limit or affect the inherent power of the High Court Division to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order under this code or to prevent abuse of the process of any court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. 

 9. The High Court Division in a proper case possesses the inherent power to quash any proceeding, judgment or to set aside decision of any court/Tribunal subordinate to it. But this power must be exercised very sparingly, cautiously and only in exceptional cases keeping in view the facts and circumstances of each and every case. The inherent power which are in the nature of extra ordinary power has to be pressed in aid when there is a flagrant abuse by subordinate court. 

 10. In this Rule the petitioner prays for quashing the proceeding of Nan O Shihsu Nirjatan case No.159 of 2008 under section 11(Gha)/ 30 of the Nan O Shishu Nirjatan Ain, 2000. 

 12. The complainant Ismat Ara Bulbul has brought case against the accused No.1 Md. Ehsanulah and others for taking and demanding dowry and for beating for dowry. On enquiry, prima facie case has been proved for which charge has been framed on 29.04.2009 against which the petitioners have brought this case under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure for quashing the proceeding. 

 13. The contention of the accused petitioners is that the opposite party No.2 had brought a CR case No.1109 of 2007 before the learned Magistrate court which was withdrawn and that she has against brought this false case again only to harassed and humiliate them. 

 14. The contention of the accused petitioner is not tenable in law because there is no bar on the part of the opposite party No.2 to bring new case on subsequently date on new grounds. The earlier case was withdraw is not a ground for quashing a proceeding. 

 15. Every case has to be decided on its own merit taking evidence. When a case is brought before a court and when a prima facie case is made out which case can not be quashed without taking evidence. Withdrawal of earlier case cannot be the ground for quashing a proceeding. 

 16. Interference under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure cannot be entertained at the primary stage of a case in sub-ordinate court. Criminal proceedings can be quashed if there is something on the record to show that the accusations in the complaint do not disclose an offence at all, or that the evidence adduced in the case discloses no offence as in that event the process of the court can be said to have been abused. The present case is not fit case for quashment in the light of the above mentioned established principle of law. The High Court would he extremely reluctant to interfere in a case where a competent court came to the view that a prima facie case is disclosed. In the instant case the trial court on enquiry has found prima facie case and on the basis of which the charge has been framed against accused persons. So there is no scope to interfere in this case. 

 17. The inherent jurisdiction is attracted firstly, 'to make such orders as may be necessary to give effect to any order of the Code'. Secondly, 'to prevent abuse of the process of any court and lastly, 'otherwise to secure the ends of justice. In the instance case, the inherent jurisdiction under the first category is not attracted. The practice of quashing the proceedings immediately after submission of the charge sheets or enquiry report has been disapproved in clear terms by the Appellate Division. Usual course of administration of criminal justice should rarely be interrupted. The FIR and the enquiry report of the case if give out certain materials and circumstances from which commission of the offence charged becomes a possibility. The High Court Division will not quash the pending proceeding on the ground that there is no evidence for the court to go upon. High Court Division is reluctant on the materials before it to go into the question of guilt or innocence of the accused under section 56IA . 

 18. Exercise of its inherent jurisdiction under section 561A by the High court depends on the facts of each case. Its interference at the initial stage of a proceeding pending before a court conditioned by the absolute necessity for such interference. But a pertinent question may be posted as to when and under what circumstances the said jurisdiction can and should be exercised by the High court. The consensus of judicial opinion is that it is not possible, desirable or expedient to lay down any inflexible rule which should govern the exercise of this inherent jurisdiction. The facts and circumstances of the present case do not deserve interference under section 561A of the Code of criminal Procedure. 

 19. The High Court should be extremely reluctant to interfere in a case where a competent court has to the view that a prima facie case is disclosed and had framed Charges. The petitioners have prayed for quashing the proceedings invoking inherent jurisdiction of this court. The power to be exercised under section 561A CR. P.C. is highly discretionary. Such an extraordinary and discretionary power cannot be exercised in favour of the persons against whom prima facie case is made out. 

 20. Law by now has been well settled that application under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure invoking the inherent jurisdiction of the High Court Division for quashing the proceeding after submission of the charge sheet or enquiry report is not maintainable. The inherent power under section 561A can be invoked at any stage of the proceedings even after conclusion of trial if it is necessary to prevent the abuse of the process of the court or otherwise to secure the ends of justice. Since the FIR and Police report disclose an offence under the Penal Code the quashment of the proceeding in the facts of the given case does not arise at all. Since the FIR disclose a prima facie case against the petitioners and to that effect the charge sheet has been submitted there is no substance in the submission made on behalf of the petitioner for quashing the proceedings. 

 21. It is reported in the case of Engineer Afsaruddin Ahmed vs. The state that a criminal case in the normal course is to be tried under the provision of Criminal procedure Code and the proceeding should not be generally interfered without at an interlocutory stage Here in this case, when prima facie case is made out it should be disputed of taking evidence and the process of case should not be hampered by invoking discretionary power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure when prima facie case has already been made out, it is appropriate to decide the matter taking evidence. In such case, if interfered it will be the gross miscarriage of justice. 

 22. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case the decisions cited we are of the view that it is not a case for interference by invoking inherent power under section 561A of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 23. In the result, the Rule is discharged. Stay granted at the time of issuance of the Rule is hereby vacated. The learned Judge, Nari o Shishu Nirjatan Tribunal is directed to proceed with the case and to disposed of the case preferably within four months from the date of receipt of this order.
